title: The Gold Ground: from a Baumgarten engraver's house to the ceiling Vienna would not hang
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Baumgarten, the birth on the Linzer Strasse
stops.date_confidence: attested; parish register of Baumgarten, then a village outside Vienna and now part of the fourteenth district
stops.campa: On the fourteenth of July 1862, in a house on the Linzer Strasse in Baumgarten, a village of small workshops and kitchen gardens beyond Vienna's walls, the gold engraver Ernst Klimt and his wife Anna have their second child. Five more will follow into the same poverty. The father's trade is the beating and cutting of gold leaf to other men's designs, badly paid in a decade when engravers are being replaced by machines. The birth house comes down in 1965 and a plaque goes up where it stood.
suggested_refs: The commemorative plaque at Linzer Strasse 247, Vienna 14, on the site of the demolished birth house
sources: Christian M. Nebehay, Gustav Klimt: Dokumentation (1969)

stops.name: Vienna, the moving rooms
stops.date_confidence: attested for the deaths and illness; the year stands for a condition running through the whole childhood, not a single day
stops.campa: The family moves rooms often through these years, one rented address to the next as the father's commissions thin. In 1874 the daughter Anna dies at five years old. Another daughter, Klara, falls into a disturbance of the mind that never lifts, and the mother carries something of the same shadow for the rest of her life. Gustav is twelve, and he draws. Within two years he is sitting the entrance examination for the new school of applied arts on the Stubenring, where the fees are waived for the sons of craftsmen.
suggested_refs: The Klimt family's successive Vienna addresses, reconstructed by Nebehay from registration records

stops.name: Kunstgewerbeschule, the scholarship on the Stubenring
stops.date_confidence: attested; Ferstel's building on the Stubenring was occupied from 1875, so the address holds for the entry year
stops.campa: At fourteen he enters the Kunstgewerbeschule, admitted on a scholarship intended for craftsmen's children rather than gentlemen's. The training is technical before it is anything else: Renaissance methods drilled by Ferdinand Laufberger and, after 1881, by Julius Victor Berger, mosaic and fresco and the copying of ornament from casts. He is meant to come out a drawing teacher. He stays seven years, longer than most students do, and leaves able to lay out a ceiling from a scaffold with no preliminary sketch to guide his hand.
suggested_refs: The Kunstgewerbeschule building, now the Universitaet fuer angewandte Kunst, Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz 2
sources: Tobias G. Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings (2012)

stops.name: Stubenring, the Kunstler-Compagnie is formed
stops.date_confidence: attested; the partnership takes joint commissions from about 1880 and the three leave the school together in 1883
stops.campa: His brother Ernst has followed him into the school in 1877, and with a fellow student, Franz Matsch, the three begin taking paid work while still enrolled: ceilings, curtains, allegorical panels, whatever a provincial building committee will pay for. They call themselves the Kunstler-Compagnie and divide each job by hand so that no single signature can be picked out of the finished plaster. In 1883 they leave the school and take a shared studio in Vienna.
suggested_refs: Contracts of the Kunstler-Compagnie, catalogued in Nebehay's documentation volume

stops.name: Reichenberg, the first ceilings for hire
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Reichenberg theatre commission is placed at the start of the partnership's independent work, and the year varies between chronologies
stops.campa: The first ceilings for hire go up in Reichenberg, a textile town in northern Bohemia whose new municipal theatre wants allegory quickly and cheaply. The work is contracted, delivered, and the scaffolding struck; neither brother has occasion to return. Over the next decade this partnership will decorate theatres and museums across the empire, its members entered on contracts as one firm rather than three. No document names which hand painted which figure.
suggested_refs: The Stadttheater at Reichenberg, now the F. X. Salda Theatre, Liberec

stops.name: Hermesvilla, a ceiling for an absent empress
stops.date_confidence: attested; the villa is built 1882-1886 and the ceiling work falls in 1884-1885
stops.campa: Deep inside the walled game park at Lainz, Empress Elisabeth is having a hunting villa built, and its interiors want ceilings. Klimt is twenty-two. He paints the salon's Der Fruehling with Franz Matsch and with his younger brother Georg, a metalworker who chases and engraves, so this job belongs to the family rather than to the Compagnie proper. The empress spends almost no time in the finished rooms. Deer are kept inside the wall for a hunt she rarely joins.
suggested_refs: Der Fruehling, salon ceiling of the Hermesvilla, by Franz Matsch with Gustav and Georg Klimt

stops.name: Fiume, the theatre on the Adriatic
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the Hungarian crown's free port on the Adriatic, the Compagnie paints ceiling decoration for the municipal theatre, one more stop in the run of provincial commissions that pays the young firm's bills through the 1880s. Klimt does not linger; the port is a job rather than a city he has come to see. The theatre is later renamed for Ivan pl. Zajc, and its ceiling stays catalogued under the Compagnie's joint name rather than under his. No painting yet carries his signature alone.
suggested_refs: Croatian National Theatre Ivan pl. Zajc, Rijeka, and its Kunstler-Compagnie ceiling
sources: Croatian National Theatre Ivan pl. Zajc archives

stops.name: Karlsbad, the spa theatre and the family joke
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The spa town's new theatre takes its ceiling from the same three hands. Karlsbad in season fills with Viennese, Russians and Germans taking the waters, and the gilt and stucco are built to receive them. Here the anonymity slips: two ceiling scenes are individually Klimt's, and in the right-hand lunette of the curtain the three painters put their own faces, with the three Klimt sisters in the lunette opposite. Whether anyone in the stalls below ever picked the faces out is not recorded.
suggested_refs: The painted curtain of the Stadttheater Karlsbad, with the self-portraits of Matsch and the Klimt brothers

stops.name: Burgtheater, the staircase and the vanished auditorium
stops.date_confidence: attested; the staircase ceilings run 1886-1888 and the Golden Cross of Merit is awarded in 1888
stops.campa: For the new Burgtheater on the Ringstrasse the Compagnie paints the staircase ceilings, the history of theatre from its beginnings forward, and Klimt is separately commissioned to record the old Burgtheater's auditorium before the wreckers reach it. He paints it from the stage, crowded with the recognisable faces of Viennese society sitting in boxes that will not exist by the time the gouache dries. Franz Joseph awards him the Golden Cross of Merit for it. In 1890 the same sheet takes the first Kaiserpreis ever given.
suggested_refs: Auditorium of the Old Burgtheater (gouache, 1888), Wien Museum

stops.name: Munich, the Glaspalast
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the German record places Klimt's Munich travel in 1888 or 1889, and the exhibition year is not fixed across sources
stops.campa: He shows at the Glaspalast, Munich's iron and glass exhibition hall built in imitation of the Crystal Palace, among painters from across Germany and Austria competing for medals he has already begun collecting at home. What survives of the trip is a line in a catalogue, with no letter or sketch beside it to say what he thought of anything hanging there. The hall burns down in 1931. Some three thousand works of the German Romantics are inside it, Caspar David Friedrich among them.
suggested_refs: Munich Glaspalast exhibition catalogues of 1888 and 1889, cited in Nebehay

stops.name: Trieste, the port on the way south
stops.date_confidence: disputed; the German record puts the Krakow, Trieste and Venice travel in 1888 or 1889, while several English accounts fold Trieste into the Italian journey of 1903
stops.campa: The journey that takes him to Munich also runs through Krakow, Trieste and Venice: the empire's main port on the Adriatic and the sea road toward Italy. Klimt passes through rather than stays; the city is a coaling stop and a railway timetable. No canvas or sketch from Trieste survives among his known work, and later writers have moved this stop forward into his famous Italian year of 1903, where it does not belong. The tour is paid for out of theatre ceilings.
suggested_refs: The 1888-1889 Krakow-Trieste-Venice-Munich itinerary as given in the German chronology

stops.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum, the spandrels above the stair
stops.date_confidence: attested; the German chronology dates the stairwell paintings from 1891, some English accounts from 1890
stops.campa: On a swaying scaffold above an unfinished stairwell, the marble not yet laid beneath him, Klimt paints spandrel and intercolumnar figures for the new Kunsthistorisches Museum on the Ringstrasse. His Ancient Greece is closer to portraiture than to emblem, a woman's face given the weight of an allegory, and it does not sit comfortably beside Matsch's stiffer neighbours. Visitors climbing the finished staircase pass under both without being told which hands did which.
suggested_refs: Ancient Greece and the intercolumnar figures of the KHM grand staircase
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Josefstadter Strasse 21, the garden studio
stops.date_confidence: attested; the German record gives the studio from 1891, some English accounts from 1892
stops.campa: He takes a garden studio behind a house in the eighth district and keeps it for twenty years. Models come and go through a courtyard door; sketchbooks accumulate by the thousand, most of them drawn for no one else's eyes. He gives almost no interviews and refuses most visitors, so what is known of the working days here comes mainly from the models themselves, questioned in old age decades afterwards. Nearly the whole of the Faculty paintings and the first gold portraits are made in this room.
stops.quote: I have never painted a self-portrait. I am less interested in myself as a subject for a painting than I am in other people, above all women.... There is nothing special about me. I am a painter who paints day after day from morning to night.... Whoever wants to know something about me ... ought to look carefully at my pictures.
stops.quote_source: Klimt, Commentary on a non-existent self-portrait, one of the few extended prose statements to survive under his name; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Gustav Klimt' (original German manuscript and date unverified)
suggested_refs: The Josefstaedter Strasse 21 garden studio, demolished; photographs in Nebehay

stops.name: Vienna, Emilie Floge
stops.date_confidence: the meeting is placed in the early 1890s, most often at 1892, through the marriage of Ernst Klimt to Helene Floge; no document fixes a first encounter
stops.campa: His brother Ernst has married Helene Floge. Helene has a younger sister, Emilie, who will build a fashion house. From the early 1890s she is the constant of Klimt's life: photographed beside him on lake jetties in loose reform dresses, painted at full length in 1902, named in his will, and never married to him. He fathers children by other women throughout. Whatever the arrangement between them is, neither of the two sets it down in writing, and the books disagree even about the kinship.
suggested_refs: Portrait of Emilie Floge (1902), Wien Museum; the Floge sisters' salon photographs

stops.name: Westbahnstrasse 36, the double bereavement
stops.date_confidence: attested; the father dies in July 1892 and the brother in December 1892
stops.campa: In July his father dies of a stroke. In December his brother Ernst dies of pericarditis at twenty-eight, leaving a widow, an infant daughter, and a firm reduced to two names. Gustav, thirty years old, becomes the support of his mother, his unmarried sisters and his brother's household, and the apartment on the Westbahnstrasse becomes the address he keeps for the rest of his life. He paints little for several years. Contemporaries date the darkening of his work to this year; he leaves no letter that says so.
suggested_refs: The Klimt family apartment at Westbahnstrasse 36, Vienna 7

stops.name: University of Vienna, the Great Hall commission
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The ministry offers the Great Hall ceiling to Franz Matsch, who cannot carry it alone; Klimt is brought in and given Philosophy, Medicine and Jurisprudence. He is thirty-two, decorated by the emperor, the safest monumental painter in Vienna. The panels are wanted as an allegory of light triumphing over darkness. What he begins instead is a column of naked bodies falling through space with no ground under them. The three panels take eleven years to deliver.
stops.quote: On the left a group of figures, the beginning of life, fruition, decay. On the right, the globe as mystery. Emerging below, a figure of light: knowledge.
stops.quote_source: Klimt describing the composition of Philosophy; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Klimt University of Vienna Ceiling Paintings'
suggested_refs: Black and white photographs of Philosophy, Medicine and Jurisprudence, the only record of the destroyed canvases
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings
en.wikipedia.org, 'Klimt University of Vienna Ceiling Paintings'

stops.name: Secession Building, the founding and the first presidency
stops.date_confidence: attested for the founding in 1897 and the opening of Olbrich's building in November 1898; the length of Klimt's presidency is contested, the German record giving 1897-1899
stops.campa: With a group of younger artists Klimt walks out of the conservative Kuenstlerhaus and founds the Vereinigung bildender Kuenstler Oesterreichs, the Secession, and is elected its first president. Joseph Maria Olbrich builds an exhibition hall by the Naschmarkt under a dome of gilded laurel leaves that Vienna promptly nicknames the golden cabbage. Over the door goes the motto: to every age its art, to art its freedom. The group's journal is called Ver Sacrum, the sacred spring, after the Roman rite in which a whole generation is vowed away.
stops.quote: Our art is not a combat of modern artists against those of the past, but the promotion of the arts against the peddlers who pose as artists and who have a commercial interest in not letting art bloom.
stops.quote_source: Hermann Bahr, first issue of Ver Sacrum, 1898; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Vienna Secession'
suggested_refs: The Secession building, Friedrichstrasse 12, Vienna, and the run of Ver Sacrum, 1898-1903

stops.name: Josefstadter Strasse 21, Nuda Veritas
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He paints a naked red-headed woman standing frontally, holding a mirror out toward whoever is looking at her. Above her head he letters a couplet of Schiller's in stylised capitals, so that the picture argues its case in words as well as in paint. Nothing here is allegory in the Ringstrasse sense: the figure is a body first and a truth second, and Vienna understands the insult exactly. Whatever the school on the Stubenring trained him to make, this is not it.
stops.quote: If you cannot please everyone with your deeds and your art, please only a few. To please many is bad.
stops.quote_source: Friedrich Schiller, inscribed by Klimt in stylised lettering above the figure of Nuda Veritas, 1899
suggested_refs: Nuda Veritas (1899), Austrian Theatre Museum, Vienna

stops.name: University of Vienna, the petition against Philosophy
stops.date_confidence: attested; Philosophy is exhibited in 1900, Medicine in 1901, Jurisprudence in 1903, and the paintings are recovered in 1905
stops.campa: Philosophy is shown before it can go up, and eighty-seven professors of the university sign a petition against it. The complaint is that the faculty has been painted as a dream of coupling and dying bodies instead of as reason. Medicine follows, with a naked pregnant woman and a Hygieia who turns her back on the sick, then Jurisprudence. The ceiling is never installed. In 1905 Klimt repays the state advance, with August Lederer's money behind him, takes the three canvases back and refuses public commissions from that day.
stops.quote: I've had enough of censorship ... I reject all state support, I don't want any of it.
stops.quote_source: Klimt, on refusing further commissions from the state; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Klimt University of Vienna Ceiling Paintings', which attaches no year to the remark
suggested_refs: The 1900 professors' petition against Philosophy, University of Vienna archives
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Klimt University of Vienna Ceiling Paintings'
Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Secession Building, the eighth exhibition
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: For the eighth exhibition the Secession gives its rooms over to the applied arts, and a complete interior by the Glasgow architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh arrives in crates and is installed inside the hall Klimt's association built. Josef Hoffmann and the men who will found the Wiener Werkstaette walk through it. The room is white, the verticals long and attenuated, with none of the Ringstrasse plush anywhere in it. What Klimt has been arguing in paint arrives in Vienna as furniture, shipped from Glasgow by a man who does not paint.
suggested_refs: The Mackintosh room at the eighth Secession exhibition, November 1900; see charles_rennie_mackintosh.journey.json

stops.name: Secession Building, the Beethoven Frieze
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: For the fourteenth exhibition, built around Max Klinger's polychrome Beethoven, Klimt paints a frieze thirty-four metres long straight onto the walls of a side gallery: casein, gold leaf and applied glass on plaster over wire mesh, made to be knocked down when the show closes. Suffering humanity, a knight in golden armour, the hostile powers, and at the end a couple folded together under a choir. Sixty thousand people come in two months. Carl Reininghaus buys the frieze to stop its demolition and it is cut off the wall in sections.
suggested_refs: The Beethoven Frieze, detached 1903, shown since 1985 in a climate-controlled basement room of the Secession, owned by the Belvedere

stops.name: Venice, the vaults of San Marco
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the spring 1903 Venice leg is attested in the chronology, but no letter or sketch fixes what he looked at there
stops.campa: In the spring he goes to Venice. The gold vaults of San Marco are the first of the two Byzantine grounds he sees this year, mosaic set so that the tesserae sit at slightly different angles and the whole wall moves when the viewer does. Venice by now is a station on every northern painter's route, walked through with a guidebook in hand. Klimt records nothing about this visit, and no sketchbook from it has been identified; the leg is reconstructed from the shape of such a journey rather than from a letter.
suggested_refs: The gold mosaic vaults of the Basilica di San Marco, Venice
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Ravenna, under the apse of San Vitale
stops.date_confidence: attested; the December 1903 Ravenna journey is the fixed point of the Italian year
stops.campa: In December he stands in San Vitale beneath the apse mosaics, Justinian and Theodora and their courts held in gold that has not moved in thirteen hundred years. There is no depth in them and no shadow, only pattern and face. He goes home to Vienna, and within four years the gold ground has appeared in his own work: in Adele Bloch-Bauer, in Danae, in the two figures of The Kiss, carried over from wall to canvas and from empire to bedroom. He leaves no diary of the trip.
suggested_refs: The apse and presbytery mosaics of the Basilica of San Vitale, Ravenna
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Palais Stoclet, the frieze drawn in Vienna
stops.date_confidence: attested; the house is built 1905-1911 and Klimt's cartoons belong to those years, though one widely repeated account dates his involvement from 1904
stops.campa: Adolphe Stoclet, a Belgian banker, commissions Josef Hoffmann to build a house on the Avenue de Tervueren and hands the entire interior to the Wiener Werkstaette. Klimt draws the dining room frieze at full size: Expectation, a dancer in profile with an Egyptian arm; Fulfilment, a couple folded into one ornamental field; and a tree of life whose spirals run the length of both walls. Leopold Forstner executes it on site in marble, enamel, coral, gold and semi-precious stone. It takes until 1911.
stops.quote: probably the ultimate stage of my development of ornament.
stops.quote_source: Klimt on the Stoclet Frieze mosaics; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Gustav Klimt'
suggested_refs: The Stoclet Frieze cartoons, Museum fuer angewandte Kunst, Vienna; the mosaics in situ at 279-281 Avenue de Tervueren

stops.name: Secession Building, walking out
stops.date_confidence: attested to 14 June 1905 by the Secession's own record; one widely circulated chronology dates the departure to 1906, conflating it with the forming of the Kunstschau group
stops.campa: On the fourteenth of June, Klimt and about half the association resign: Hoffmann, Koloman Moser, Carl Moll, the group that wants the applied arts and the Werkstaette treated as the equals of painting, against the members who want the Secession to remain a painters' club. He walks out of the building whose motto he wrote over the door, eight years after founding it. He holds no formal office in an art institution again. The group that gathers around him afterwards is known simply as the Klimt Group.
suggested_refs: The resignation of the Klimt Group from the Vienna Secession, 14 June 1905

stops.name: Elisabethstrasse, the portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer
stops.date_confidence: attested; painted 1903-1907
stops.campa: Ferdinand Bloch-Bauer, a sugar industrialist, has commissioned a portrait of his wife Adele, and it takes three years and more than a hundred preparatory drawings. Klimt paints her face and hands and dissolves everything else into gold and silver leaf, eyes and triangles and spirals, until the woman is a mosaic with a living head on it. She is the only sitter he paints twice in finished oil. She dies in 1925 at forty-three. The picture is taken from the family by the Nazi state in 1941 and not returned until 2006.
suggested_refs: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I (1907), Neue Galerie New York, restituted to Maria Altmann in 2006
sources: Neue Galerie New York provenance record

stops.name: Kunstschau, the pavilion on the Lothringerstrasse
stops.date_confidence: attested; the exhibition runs 1 June to 16 November 1908
stops.campa: Shut out of the Secession he founded, Klimt builds his own exhibition on empty ground at the Lothringerstrasse: a temporary wooden pavilion designed by Hoffmann, with one room given to Klimt and sixteen of his paintings hung in it. Among them are two figures kneeling in a field of gold, catalogued as Liebespaar, which the state gallery buys unfinished before the show closes. In the Vienna winter just past a twenty-year-old Swiss, Charles-Edouard Jeanneret, has met him among the men arguing ornament into a moral question.
suggested_refs: The Kiss (Der Kuss), bought as Liebespaar at the 1908 Kunstschau, Belvedere, Vienna
le_corbusier.journey.json, the Vienna winter of 1907-1908

stops.name: Florence, the quattrocento gold
stops.date_confidence: attested in the German chronology, which places Florence visits in 1908 and 1911; several biographies wrongly fold Florence into the 1903 itinerary
stops.campa: He goes to Florence, where the gold is quattrocento panel gold, laid flat behind saints who stand on nothing. It is the same refusal of depth he carried out of Ravenna, arrived at four centuries earlier by other means and with a different theology behind it. Biographers have moved this visit back to 1903 to make the Italian journey tidier, and the tidier version is the one that circulates. The German record puts him in Florence in 1908 and again in 1911. He writes nothing about either stay, and no picture is dated from either.
suggested_refs: Quattrocento gold-ground panels of the Uffizi and the Museo di San Marco, Florence
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Toledo, El Greco with Carl Moll
stops.date_confidence: the Spanish journey with Carl Moll is attested; the influence read from it is contested between biographers
stops.campa: With Carl Moll he travels to Spain, to Madrid and to Toledo, where El Greco is being rediscovered by exactly the circles Klimt moves in. The elongated figures, the acid greens and violets, bodies stretched past anatomy into flame. Whether this changes his own late manner is argued both ways: the angular, brittle, unglazed figures of his last decade are read by some as El Greco's mark and by others as ordinary ageing. Both readings rest on the pictures alone; he never wrote about El Greco.
suggested_refs: The El Greco paintings of Toledo, seen on the 1909 Spanish journey
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Paris, after the gold
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Paris leg of the 1909 journey is given in the chronology, and the stylistic reading attached to it is interpretive
stops.campa: On the same journey he stops in Paris. The city has moved past the gold ground he has spent a decade perfecting, and the Kunstschau of that year has already brought Van Gogh, Munch and Matisse into direct comparison with Viennese work back home. After this trip his painting loosens: brighter, flatter, patterned with folk colour instead of metal. How much of that is Paris and how much is the ordinary exhaustion of a manner, no source can say. No source dates the end of the gold phase more closely than to these months.
suggested_refs: The international section of the 1909 Kunstschau, Vienna, with Van Gogh, Munch and Matisse
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Rome, first prize at the Valle Giulia
stops.date_confidence: the prize is attested; Klimt's personal attendance at the Rome opening is not confirmed in any surviving correspondence
stops.campa: Death and Life takes the first prize for painting at the international exhibition in Rome, held in the new pavilions at the Valle Giulia built for the fiftieth anniversary of Italian unification. A sleeping heap of human bodies at one side, a grinning skeleton in a patterned robe at the other, and nothing between them. Whether Klimt is in the room when the prize is announced no letter records. Four years later he takes the picture down and repaints its ground.
suggested_refs: Death and Life (1910-1915), Leopold Museum, Vienna

stops.name: Brussels, the frieze seen in place
stops.date_confidence: disputed; the visit to the completed frieze is usually dated 1914, while one account places his inspection around 1910-1911
stops.campa: He goes to Brussels to see the dining room finished: the frieze he drew in Vienna nine years earlier, executed in stone and metal by other hands, in a house he has never yet stood inside. It is the only work of his that exists as architecture rather than as a picture, and the only one he cannot take back off a wall and repaint. The Stoclet family keeps the house private, and for a century afterwards almost nobody outside it sees the frieze in place. He is in the room with it for a matter of days.
suggested_refs: Palais Stoclet, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2009 partly on the strength of the Klimt frieze

stops.name: Villa Paulick, the first Attersee summer
stops.date_confidence: attested; the German record gives regular Attersee summers from 1900 to 1916, largely at the Villa Paulick in Seewalchen, and corrects older accounts placing the first summer in the 1890s
stops.campa: The first Attersee summer. Klimt stays with the Floge family at the Paulick villa in Seewalchen, at the lake's northern end, and begins painting water. The canvases come out square, a format he keeps for nearly all the landscapes, so the shoreline can sit anywhere in the frame or stay out of it altogether. He works from the boathouse and from a rowing boat, using a telescope and a cut cardboard viewfinder to isolate the slice he wants before any paint is mixed. The locals call him the Waldschrat, the forest demon.
suggested_refs: Villa Paulick, Seewalchen am Attersee, and its boathouse

stops.name: Litzlberg, the keep on the water
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Litzlberg summers; older accounts misplace Litzlberg on the eastern shore, and it lies on the west, in the municipality of Seewalchen
stops.campa: Litzlberg, a wooded point on the western shore, with a ruined keep on an island just offshore that he paints repeatedly. The Attersee pictures sell more easily than the figure paintings and cause no scandal whatever, a second practice running quietly beside the one making headlines in Vienna. Photographs from these years show him barefoot on a jetty in a loose linen smock, a different man from the one photographed in a stiff collar in the Josefstaedter studio.
suggested_refs: Schloss Litzlberg and the island keep, Attersee, subject of several Klimt canvases

stops.name: Schloss Kammer, the castle painted from the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Schloss Kammer canvases belong to the summers of about 1908-1912
stops.campa: Across several summers he paints the moated castle at Kammer from the water, four related canvases in which the lake surface climbs until it has swallowed most of the frame and the building is a pale mass above its own reflection. The castle stands on a peninsula at the lake's northern end. He works outdoors daily, in a place where nothing is commissioned and no professor can sign a petition, painting the same object again and again until it comes apart into pattern.
suggested_refs: The four Schloss Kammer canvases, 1908-1912; the Gustav Klimt Zentrum at Kammerl, Schoerfling am Attersee
sources: Natter, Gustav Klimt: The Complete Paintings

stops.name: Weissenbach, the forester's house
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1914-1916 by the local record, which corrects chronologies giving 1912-1914
stops.campa: For three summers he rents rooms in a forester's house at Weissenbach, at the lake's steep southern end, where the water narrows between wooded slopes. He paints the house itself twice, and across the water the church at Unterach, still working the square format he settled on fourteen years earlier. Local memory, collected decades afterwards by regional historians, has him swimming every morning before the light was any good for painting. No photograph confirms it.
suggested_refs: The Forsthaus at Weissenbach, a locality of Steinbach am Attersee, painted twice by Klimt

stops.name: Weissenbach, the last summer at the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested as the last dated Attersee stay
stops.campa: The last Attersee summer, again at Weissenbach, the routine of sixteen years holding while the war narrows what reaches the lake: less coffee, less paint, fewer guests in the villas that used to fill each July. He is fifty-four. He rows out for the view, works the same square canvases he has worked since 1900, and sends the short postcards to Vienna that he has always sent from this lake. Nothing in his letters marks the season as any different from the fifteen before it.
suggested_refs: The 1916 Attersee canvases, the last of the landscape series

stops.name: Feldmuhlgasse 11, the last studio
stops.date_confidence: attested; the move from the Josefstaedter Strasse is dated 1911 or 1912 depending on the chronology
stops.campa: He moves the studio to a garden house in Hietzing, near Schoenbrunn, a few rooms and an orchard behind a wall. He keeps Japanese prints and Chinese robes there for models to wear, cats in the yard, potted plants, and a photographic apparatus. Egon Schiele comes as a younger colleague rather than a rival, and the two are photographed together on the property. The house survives the century. Its studio rooms open to the public on the thirtieth of September 2012.
suggested_refs: The Klimt Villa, Feldmuehlgasse 11, Vienna 13, with the reconstructed studio rooms

stops.name: Westbahnstrasse 36, the mother's death and the repainted ground
stops.date_confidence: attested for Anna Klimt's death in 1915 and for the reworking of Death and Life in the same year
stops.campa: His mother Anna dies. Klimt is fifty-three and has kept her and his unmarried sisters since 1892. In the same year he takes Death and Life back off the wall and repaints its ground, killing the gold and setting mosaic elements into what replaces it, so that a picture already given a first prize in Rome becomes a different picture with the same title and the same date on the wall label. The accounts disagree about the colour he put there. The German record says grey, others say blue, others black.
suggested_refs: Death and Life in its 1915 state, Leopold Museum, Vienna

stops.name: Feldmuhlgasse 11, the unfinished portraits
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The late portraits are made here: the Lady with a Fan, Amalie Zuckerkandl, the Bride, Adam and Eve. Many will be found on their easels unfinished, faces resolved and bodies still drawn in charcoal under thin colour, so that the method is visible in a way it never is in a completed picture: the head first, everything else negotiable. The gold is gone. The grounds are flat colour and folk pattern now, borrowed from embroidery and from the Chinese and Japanese things stacked around the walls.
suggested_refs: The Bride and Adam and Eve, left unfinished in the Feldmuehlgasse studio; Alice Strobl's catalogue raisonne of the drawings
sources: Alice Strobl, Gustav Klimt: Die Zeichnungen (1980-1989)

stops.name: Westbahnstrasse 36, the stroke
stops.date_confidence: attested; both standard chronologies give 11 January 1918, although one account describes the date as disputed
stops.campa: On the eleventh of January he suffers a stroke in the Westbahnstrasse apartment. It paralyses the right side of his body, which is the painting side. He has lived at this address since the year his father and his brother died, twenty-six years in the same rooms, and he is moved out of them to the general hospital the same day. One account calls the date uncertain and offers alternatives a few days earlier. The two standard chronologies agree on the eleventh.
suggested_refs: The Westbahnstrasse 36 apartment, Klimt's home address from 1892 to 1918

stops.name: Allgemeines Krankenhaus, the sixth of February
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He dies at the general hospital on the Alser Strasse, pneumonia following the stroke inside the influenza wave then moving through Vienna and most of Europe. He is fifty-five, and the four weeks between the stroke and the death are the only weeks of his adult life in which he does not work. Egon Schiele draws his face on the deathbed, one of the last images made of it, and dies of the same pandemic on the thirty-first of October, three days after his pregnant wife.
stops.quote_source: Reported last words of Gustav Klimt after his stroke, given secondhand; quoted in Wikipedia, 'Emilie Floege'. No document in Klimt's own hand records them.
suggested_refs: Egon Schiele's deathbed drawing of Klimt, 1918

stops.name: Hietzinger Friedhof, the grave in group five
stops.date_confidence: attested; honorary grave, group 5, number 194
stops.campa: He is buried in the Hietzing cemetery, a short walk from the Feldmuehlgasse studio, under a plain stone with a name and two dates and none of the gold on it. Vienna in February 1918 is nine months from the end of the empire whose emperor decorated him at twenty-six. The Faculty paintings, bought back and never installed, are still in private hands. In May 1945 ten of his works burn at Schloss Immendorf in Lower Austria, and who set that fire is still argued.
suggested_refs: Honorary grave of Gustav Klimt, Hietzinger Friedhof, Maxingstrasse 15, group 5 no. 194
The Schloss Immendorf fire of 8 May 1945, attribution questioned by Tina Maria Storkovich
